chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about gold: 'How much zakat is in it?' He said: 'When its value reaches two hundred dirhams, then zakat is due upon it.'

key_terms.الذَّهَب: Gold; one of two monetary metals on which zakat is obligatory in Islamic law
key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat; the obligatory alms-tax, one of the Five Pillars of Islam
key_terms.قِيمَة: Value/price; the monetary worth used to determine the zakat threshold for gold
key_terms.مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ: Two hundred dirhams; the nisab (minimum threshold) for silver zakat, here used as the value benchmark for gold

ai.seo_question: What is the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on gold according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the most prolific companions of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) who transmitted some 30,000 hadiths, poses a direct jurisprudential question about the zakat threshold for gold. The Imam establishes that zakat on gold is triggered when the gold's monetary value reaches the equivalent of two hundred silver dirhams — the same threshold as the nisab for silver. This ruling links the two precious metals through a shared monetary standard rather than separate weight calculations, reflecting the early Islamic monetary system in which dirhams served as the primary unit of value.
